intro: Protects home buyers from builder delays, hidden changes and misused money. Every state has a RERA authority — in Tamil Nadu, TNRERA. Check a project's registration on the state RERA website before booking.

sections.p: A builder can't advertise, book or sell flats or plots in a project without registering it with RERA, if the land is over 500 sq m or it has more than 8 units. Agents must register too (S 9).
sections.pen: S 59: up to 10% of project cost; more for continued violation

sections.p: 70% of money collected from buyers must go into a separate bank account and be used only for that project's construction and land cost.
The builder must update the project's RERA web page with sanctioned plans, approvals, progress and booking status.
The builder can't take more than 10% of the price as advance or application fee before signing a registered agreement for sale.

The builder can't change sanctioned plans or specifications without your consent (and two-thirds of allottees for common areas). Structural defects or poor workmanship reported within 5 years of possession must be fixed free within 30 days, failing which you get compensation.
Flats must be sold on carpet area — the usable floor area inside the walls — not on inflated 'super built-up' area.

If the builder fails to hand over possession on the promised date, you can choose to withdraw and get a full refund with interest and compensation, or stay in the project and get interest for every month of delay.
Right to information about plans and schedule, to possession on time, to necessary documents and plans, and to have the residents' association formed and common areas handed over.
File complaints online with the state RERA Authority (or its adjudicating officer for compensation). Appeals go to the Real Estate Appellate Tribunal within 60 days (S 44).
